label: ARMADA system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses an ARMADA YprA-like-helicase locus whose Type I and Type II operons share BrxHII-like and PglX-like components with DISARM Class I systems and whose experimentally tested Type II forms protect against a broad range of phages.
observations: DefenseFinder article-registry branch under phage defense system; distinct from individual ArmA, ArmB, ArmC, and ArmD proteins, the broader YprA helicase family, narrower ARMADA Type I or Type II subtype traits, E. coli NCTC 12900 and ATCC 8739 locus instances, absent pinned DefenseFinder HMM-profile rows, the absent pinned DefenseFinder rule row, exact PADLOC custom model boundaries, direct phage triggers or effector outputs, co-encoded Druantia or Zorya systems, SPIDER mobile elements, and other phage-defense systems.
